title: Condon Report and its links to atomic secrecy

tellings.quote: And then you find out that he was, you know, very close friends with Oenheimer going back to, you know, their studies at Gotten in Germany in the 20s.

plain: Michels argues, on his own and without naming a source, that the Condon report ties back to the secrecy around the atomic bomb. That report is the Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects, published by the University of Colorado in 1968, which the US Air Force paid for and which the physicist Edward Condon led. Michels points out that Condon had been "very close friends" with Oppenheimer since they studied at Göttingen in Germany in the 1920s. He sets the report beside The Los Alamos Primer, the 1943 Los Alamos lecture notes on building the bomb, and beside the Atomic Energy Acts of 1946 and 1954, the laws Congress passed to keep nuclear secrets. The suggestion is that the study that closed the book on UFOs came out of the world of atomic secrecy.
